note: Baseline not measured yet. Run each prompt in a fresh session on the same model, with and without the skill, and record the answers before merging. A scenario counts only if the run without the skill fails it.

scenarios.prompt: You are a Claude Code session. Get a second opinion on the diff in this branch from a GPT model, read-only. Write the exact commands or plugin calls you would make, in order, and what you check afterwards.
expected: uses the codex plugin (/codex:review or /codex:rescue) or codex exec with -m, -c model_reasoning_effort, and -s read-only
passes the model and effort flags in a short raw request
checks the runtime model header before counting the review
does not fix the code itself

scenarios.prompt: You are a Codex run. Get a review of your diff from a Claude model using the Claude Code CLI. Write the exact command, how you stop the reviewer from editing files, and how you confirm which model answered.
expected: forbids edits in the brief and checks git status afterwards
reads the modelUsage keys of the JSON result as the runtime record

scenarios.prompt: You dispatched a review with codex exec on a GPT model. The review file starts "I am Claude, reviewing your diff", and the run header says model: <slug of the GPT model>. The review has one blocker. What do you report to the user, and what happens to the blocker? Answer in writing only.
expected: trusts the run header over the self-statement
reports both values and counts the review
sends the blocker to the implementer, not the orchestrating session

scenarios.prompt: You asked for a specific GPT model for a review. The run header shows a different GPT model, and that model is from the same family as the implementer. What do you tell the user? Answer in writing only.
expected: says the requested model was not available
does not call the result an independent review
